Ordering/Treating Surgeon: [Okafor, MD — full name, NPI, and contact number not provided in the records shared with me]

To the Appeals Review Committee:

I am writing to formally appeal the denial of prior authorization for CPT 29827 (rotator cuff repair) dated 2026-08-18. The stated reason for denial was that "the documentation submitted was incomplete and does not allow a determination of medical necessity." I am submitting this appeal, together with my treating surgeon's clinical records, to address that stated deficiency and to request that the determination be reversed.

**Identification of the applicable clinical criteria**

Based on my own research, Anthem's musculoskeletal prior-authorization reviews (including for shoulder arthroscopy/rotator cuff repair) are generally conducted under clinical appropriateness criteria published by Carelon Medical Benefits Management (formerly AIM Specialty Health) in its guideline titled "Musculoskeletal Appropriate Use Criteria: Joint Surgery," Doc ID MSK02‑1125.1, effective 11/15/2025. I was able to locate and directly retrieve only limited excerpts of the rotator‑cuff‑repair criteria in that document; I was not able to obtain the complete text of every criterion. I am not certain this is the precise document your reviewer applied to my claim, since the denial notice itself does not identify a specific policy title, number, or section. **I am formally requesting, as part of this appeal, that you identify by name and number the exact medical policy or clinical guideline used to deny this request, and provide me with a complete copy of the criteria applied**, so that I can respond point-by-point if any gap remains.

To the extent the Carelon "Joint Surgery" guideline is what was applied, the only text of that document I was able to directly verify (and which I therefore quote here, rather than paraphrase) is the following, describing the pathway for a non-traumatic, gradually developing tear — which matches my clinical presentation:

"Rotator cuff repair is considered medically necessary for a chronic or degenerative full thickness tear when ALL the following criteria are met: Gradual onset of shoulder pain in the absence of a significant traumatic event within the preceding 3 months"

"Pain ≥ 3 on the VAS scale which …" [this fragment was cut off in the source I retrieved; I do not have the remainder of this sentence and am not quoting or guessing at it]

I was not able to retrieve the remaining criteria elements (if any) for this specific pathway (e.g., any additional imaging, physical-exam, or conservative-care sub-requirements), and I do not attribute any further plan language to Anthem or Carelon beyond what is quoted above. Below, I address each element I was able to verify, and I separately present — in my own words, clearly not as quoted plan language — the clinical facts I believe are relevant to demonstrating medical necessity, so that the reviewer can match them against whatever complete criteria set was actually used.

**1. Non-traumatic, gradual-onset presentation ("Gradual onset of shoulder pain in the absence of a significant traumatic event within the preceding 3 months")**
My symptoms developed progressively over approximately 14 months, without any discrete traumatic injury. This is documented in my surgeon's clinical notes. This appears to place my case in the "chronic or degenerative" pathway quoted above, rather than an acute traumatic tear.

**2. Pain severity**
The retrieved plan-language fragment references a minimum VAS pain score, but the numeric threshold and the remainder of that sentence were not available to me. My records document progressive pain that prevents me from lifting my arm above shoulder height and from sleeping on the affected side, and document positive provocative testing and pain-limited range of motion on exam. [A specific numeric VAS pain score does not appear to be recorded in the packet provided to me — if one exists in the surgeon's chart, it should be submitted as an addendum; if not, I am requesting that my surgeon supply one before the appeal is decided.]

**3. Diagnostic confirmation of a full-thickness tear**
MRI of the shoulder dated 2026-06-15 confirms a full-thickness supraspinatus tear measuring 1.8 cm, with grade 2 fatty atrophy. This directly documents the "full thickness tear" referenced in the quoted criterion above.

**4. Functional impairment**
I am unable to lift my arm above shoulder height or sleep on the affected side, and my exam shows pain-limited range of motion and positive provocative testing on the affected side. I present this as clinical evidence of significant functional impairment; I am not aware of, and am not quoting, any specific plan-language functional-impairment threshold, because I was not able to retrieve one for this pathway.

**5. Failed conservative management**
Prior to requesting surgery, I completed an extensive, well-documented course of conservative treatment:
- Supervised physical therapy focused on rotator cuff strengthening and scapular mechanics: 16 weeks, from 2026-04-06 to 2026-07-27, 24 visits completed, as documented in the physical therapy discharge note.
- NSAIDs for 6 months, with inadequate relief.
- Corticosteroid injection on 2026-06-02, which provided only 4 weeks of partial relief.

I present this treatment history as evidence of failed conservative management. I was not able to retrieve a specific numeric conservative-care duration requirement (e.g., "6 weeks" or another threshold) that is confirmed to apply to the chronic/degenerative full-thickness tear pathway specifically, so I am not asserting that any particular plan-stated duration was met — only that my actual conservative treatment (16 weeks of supervised PT, 6 months of NSAIDs, and an injection) is extensive and well documented, and I am asking the reviewer to confirm against the complete criteria whether this satisfies the applicable duration requirement.

**6. Absence of contraindications**
My records show no active infection, no untreated substance use, a BMI of 29, and no tobacco use. I identified through my research that the guideline's rotator cuff repair section contains a list of contraindications, but I was not able to retrieve the specific contraindication list itself, so I am not quoting it. Based on the facts above, I am not aware of any contraindication that would apply to me, and I ask the reviewer to confirm this against the complete list.

**Response to the stated denial reason**

The denial states only that "documentation was incomplete," without specifying which document(s) or data element(s) were missing. As shown above, the prior authorization packet already contains: (1) a symptom history and duration, (2) a formal MRI report confirming a full-thickness tear with fatty atrophy grading, (3) a physical therapy discharge note documenting 24 completed visits over 16 weeks, (4) documentation of a 6-month NSAID trial, (5) documentation of a corticosteroid injection and its outcome, and (6) surgeon's exam findings including positive provocative testing and functional limitations. Given the specificity and completeness of this record, I am requesting that the plan identify precisely what additional documentation is believed to be missing so that it can be promptly supplied, and that the plan reconsider its determination in light of the records enclosed with this appeal.

**Requested action**

1. Reverse the denial and approve prior authorization for CPT 29827.
2. If the denial is not fully reversed on this record, identify — in writing and by specific policy section/criterion — exactly what documentation or clinical finding is considered missing.
3. Provide a complete copy of the specific medical policy or clinical guideline (title, number, and effective date) actually applied to this determination.
4. Offer my treating surgeon, Dr. Okafor, a peer-to-peer review opportunity before any final appeal decision is issued.

**Enclosures**
- Physical therapy discharge note (2026-04-06 to 2026-07-27, 24 visits)
- MRI report, shoulder, dated 2026-06-15
- Medication/injection records (NSAID trial; corticosteroid injection 2026-06-02)
- Surgeon's clinic notes documenting symptom duration, functional limitation, and physical exam findings
- [Any additional records the surgeon's office deems relevant, including a numeric pain score if available]
- Copy of the Notice of Adverse Benefit Determination dated 2026-08-18

I understand this appeal must be received by 2027-02-14, as stated in the denial notice, and I am submitting it well within that timeframe. Please confirm receipt of this appeal in writing and advise of the expected timeline for a decision.

Thank you for your prompt attention to this matter.

Sincerely,

Emerson Foster
